G1_all_learn.rule: every fine-tune (4 tasks x 2 seeds) reaches held-out P(target) >= 0.5 within 300 steps; a state that does not is dropped from every class range and the round is flagged

G2_lift_exact.rule: the lifted state's target model has the fine-tune's held-out P(target) to 1e-3 and its route shares sum to 1 to 1e-6, on every state

G3_random_null.rule: a Gaussian delta-W with the fine-tune's per-matrix norms reads pooled inexpressible share / isotropic null within [0.9, 1.1] on every state

P1_inexpressible.blind_to: whether the expressible part does anything (round 2: the inexpressible part alone also partly carries the behaviour)
P1_inexpressible.number: pooled input-weighted inexpressible share of the fine-tune's delta-W / its isotropic null (harness.inexpressible_of)

P2_residual_share.number: e_delta of the Euclidean-lifted state: the share of the held-out log-odds gain at the trigger that stays in Delta
P2_residual_share.rule: does NOT separate (the key-value round read 0.13 identity, 0.18 random, 0.13 one-pair random)

P3_relevance_W0.blind_to: for the new tasks W0's target probability is ~1e-6, so k_lo near 1 is also what no signal reads; the random sets' spread is the floor. Reported beside: the KL version (k_kl), and the same ablations in the fine-tuned model (does T carry the trained behaviour)
P3_relevance_W0.control: the random sets give 1 by construction
P3_relevance_W0.number: k_lo = |mean drop of W0's target log-odds at the trigger when T (the 100 subcomponents the lift moves most) is ablated| / mean |drop| over 5 random sets matched per matrix on size and on the decile of CI at the trigger
P3_relevance_W0.rule: separates, existing higher (expected existing k_lo >= 3, new within 0.5-2). Indicative: depends on |T| = 100 and the matching, both fixed here

P4_route.blind_to: the update itself; it reads how frozen Gamma routes the trained model at the trigger
P4_route.number: r (re-switching share) and e_gate (masked-off share) of the lifted state
P4_route.rule: both separate: r existing higher (expected >= 0.6 vs <= 0.35), e_gate new higher (expected >= 0.45 vs <= 0.25). The positive control of the round: if this does not separate on the new seeds and tasks, the round has no power

P5_seed_consistency.blind_to: what produces the behaviour: it compares which subcomponents moved most (the recruit test's lesson)
P5_seed_consistency.number: Jaccard of T between the two fine-tune seeds of a task (2 values per class)
P5_seed_consistency.rule: separates, existing higher (expected existing >= 0.5); Jaccard of S_on reported beside

reported_not_scored: T's mean CI at the trigger at W0 and under the trained activations (existing higher expected)
Gamma coverage of the task gradient at W0 (existing higher expected; the ladder found it does not predict d)
lift energy on subcomponents switched off at the trigger in the trained model (new higher expected)
T's and S_on's on-rate over Pile at W0 against the alive mean (new tasks' T rarer expected)
identity tasks: Jaccard of S_on and T with the top-100 'repeat the current token' subcomponents on Pile (>= 0.2 expected against ~0.01 for a random set)
sizes of S_on and S_off and mean |dg| at the trigger
do-nothing route split (r only; the G3-style identity check)
scored_step_rule: per fine-tune, the first checkpoint (10, 30, 100, 300) with held-out P(target) >= 0.5; else the last checkpoint, flagged 'did not learn'. The scored step and ||delta-W||/||W0|| are recorded beside every number (a step difference between the classes is a confound to check, not a match)
separation_rule: a number separates the classes when the two classes' ranges (one value per fine-tuned state: 4 per class; for the across-seed numbers one per task: 2 per class) do not overlap AND the gap between the ranges exceeds the larger within-class range; the predicted direction must hold
